sources.citation: Ubels, Edward H. 1983. Mood and aspect in Karang. Studies in African Linguistics 14(1): 47-70. DOI 10.32473/sal.v14i1.107535
sources.access_detail: copy on file; access check: open copy online (also: harvard online access (harvardkey))
sources.note: Section 1.1 'Phonology and morphology of the verb' (p. 49) and fn. 2 describe tone only: every verb root carries one tone, two tone classes (mid, low), orthography marks high/low/rising with mid unmarked; the words 'stress' and 'accent' do not occur anywhere in the article. Refers the reader to Ubels & Ubels 1980 for the phonology.

sources.citation: Wikipedia, 'Karang language' (citing Ethnologue 18th ed. 2015; Binam Bikoi ed. 2012 ALCAM)
sources.note: Nothing on stress; notes the orthography marks high tone with an acute accent; dialects Karang and Ngumi; related varieties Sakpu, Nzakmbay, Mbere.

sources.citation: PHOIBLE 2.0 inventory AA 744 'karaŋ' (contributors Chanard 2006 / Hartell ed. 1993, Alphabets of Africa)
sources.note: Segment inventory (40 segments) only; no stress or tone statement.

Nothing on stress; lists Ubels & Ubels 1980 (pp. 1-5, classification), Glidden 1985 (Koh verbal system, actually about Kuo [xuo]), Elders 2006, Bennett 1983, Boyd & Pasch 1988, Campbell et al. 2022; alternative names Eastern Mbum, Lakka, Mbum Bakal, Nzák Kàráng.
